paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the performance of two methods—ST-ES (blue line with circular markers) and Random (orange line with circular markers)—in terms of minFDE₂₀ as the number of in-context examples varies from 0 to 8. The x-axis is labeled “Number of Examples” and ranges from 0 to 8 with linear spacing and integer tick labels at each unit. The y-axis is labeled “minFDE₂₀ (↑)”, indicating a higher value is better, and ranges from 17 to 24 with linear spacing and tick marks at every unit. For the ST-ES method, the minFDE₂₀ starts at approximately 21.6 when no examples are provided, drops steeply to around 18.2 at 1 example, then continues to decrease gradually to about 17.3 at 6 examples, stabilizing around 17.4 for 7 and 8 examples. For the Random method, the minFDE₂₀ begins at approximately 23.8 with 0 examples, decreases to about 22.3 at 1 example, then stabilizes around 21.8 to 22.0 for 2 through 8 examples, showing minimal improvement beyond 1 example. Both lines are solid, and the legend indicates the methods with corresponding colors and markers.
model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates the performance of two methods—ST-ES (blue line with circular markers) and Random (orange line with circular markers)—in terms of minFDE₂₀ (in meters) as the number of in-context examples varies from 0 to 8. The x-axis, labeled "Number of Examples," is linear and ranges from 0 to 8, with tick marks at integer intervals. The y-axis, labeled "minFDE₂₀ (→)", is also linear and ranges from 17 to 24, with tick marks at 1-unit intervals. The ST-ES method starts at a minFDE₂₀ of approximately 21.2 when 0 examples are provided, then decreases sharply to around 18.0 at 1 example, and stabilizes between 17.4 and 17.6 for 2 to 8 examples. The Random method begins at a higher minFDE₂₀ of approximately 23.8 with 0 examples, decreases gradually to about 22.0 at 2 examples, and then remains nearly constant between 21.8 and 22.0 for 4 to 8 examples. The blue line for ST-ES consistently lies below the orange line for Random across all example counts, indicating better performance.
